title: Embedded digit-writing machine
statement: For any types $Q$ and $T$ with decidable equality, there are a natural number $K$, a finite state set $S$ with decidable equality, a machine $R$ with $K+1$ work tapes over symbols encoding digits, marked work cells, states, or tags, designated states $entry,exit\in S$, and a natural number $C$. For every $k$, embedding $\iota:\{0,\ldots,K\}\hookrightarrow\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, Boolean word $x$, and initial configuration $a$ of $R$ on input $x$, suppose $a$ is in state $entry$, its input head is at position $1$, all its work-tape cells are blank, and its output is empty. For any surrounding tapes, head positions, and output prefix, embed this computation into the $k$-tape machine; then at some time $t\le C(|x|+1)$ it reaches the corresponding embedded configuration with state $exit$ and the binary expansion of $|x|+1$ written on tape $\iota(0)$ from its initial head position. It does not visit $exit$ earlier, and every work-tape head remains within distance $C(\operatorname{bits}(|x|+1)+1)$ of its initial position through time $t$.
